881	    def _split_train_data_by_dp(self, data):
882	        """Compute the DP/mbs schedule and package each rank's rollout_data
883	        into a Ray Box. The schedule itself is computed by
884	        :func:`build_dp_schedule` so it stays unit-testable without Ray/sglang.
885	
886	        Step split is by rollout id (``samples[i].rollout_id``, falling back
887	        to ``samples[i].index``); each step holds exactly
888	        ``args.global_batch_size`` rollouts so the training-step count per
889	        rollout is fixed at ``rollout_batch_size * n_samples_per_prompt //
890	        global_batch_size`` regardless of how many training samples each
891	        rollout produced.
892	        """
893	        dp_size = self.train_parallel_config["dp_size"]
894	        total_lengths = [len(t) for t in data["tokens"]]
895	        data["total_lengths"] = total_lengths
896	
897	        partitions, micro_batch_indices, num_microbatches, global_batch_sizes = build_dp_schedule(
898	            self.args,
899	            self.train_parallel_config,
900	            total_lengths,
901	            global_batch_size=self.args.global_batch_size,
902	            rollout_indices=data["rollout_ids"],
903	        )
904	
905	        # Package per-rank rollout_data
906	        rollout_data_refs = []
907	        for r in range(dp_size):
908	            partition = partitions[r]
909	            rollout_data = {"partition": partition}
910	            for key in [
911	                "tokens",
912	                "multimodal_train_inputs",
913	                "response_lengths",
914	                "rewards",
915	                "truncated",
916	                "loss_masks",
917	                "round_number",
918	                "sample_indices",
919	                "rollout_ids",
920	                "rollout_mask_sums",
921	                "rollout_log_probs",
922	                "rollout_top_p_token_ids",
923	                "rollout_top_p_token_offsets",
924	                "rollout_routed_experts",
925	                "source_names",
926	                "prompt",
927	                "teacher_log_probs",
928	            ]:
929	                if key not in data:
930	                    continue
931	                rollout_data[key] = [data[key][j] for j in partition]
932	            # keys that need to be splited at train side
933	            for key in ["raw_reward", "total_lengths"]:
934	                if key not in data:
935	                    continue
936	                rollout_data[key] = data[key]
937	            rollout_data["global_batch_sizes"] = global_batch_sizes
938	            rollout_data["num_microbatches"] = num_microbatches
939	            rollout_data["micro_batch_indices"] = micro_batch_indices[r]
940	            _tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(rollout_data)
941	            transport = getattr(self.args, "rollout_data_transport", "object-store")
942	            if transport == "nixl":
943	                rollout_data_refs.append(Box(ray.put(rollout_data, _tensor_transport="nixl")))
944	            elif transport == "object-store":
945	                rollout_data_refs.append(Box(ray.put(rollout_data)))
946	            else:
947	                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout data transport: {transport!r}")
948	        return rollout_data_refs

951	def _validate_rollout_id_annotated(node, depth=0):
952	    """Walk the rollout function's nested output and validate ``rollout_id`` only
953	    when a compact / subagent pattern is detected.
954	
955	    "Compact" = the rollout function wraps multiple training samples from one
956	    rollout execution into a ``list[Sample]``. In slime's convention the
957	    default rollout shape is ``list[list[Sample]]`` (depth-2: prompt × rollout)
958	    so its leaf ``list[Sample]`` lands at depth 1 and we skip validation,
959	    preserving backward compatibility. A compact rollout adds a third level:
960	    ``list[list[list[Sample]]]`` (prompt × rollout × samples-from-one-rollout),
961	    so the leaf ``list[Sample]`` lands at depth ≥ 2. At that point we require
962	    every sibling to carry a non-None ``rollout_id`` and to share the same
963	    value, so the loss reducer counts the rollout once instead of N times.
964	    """
965	    if isinstance(node, Sample):
966	        return
967	    assert isinstance(node, list), f"unexpected rollout output node type: {type(node).__name__}"
968	    if node and isinstance(node[0], Sample):
969	        if depth >= 2 and len(node) > 1:
970	            rids = [s.rollout_id for s in node]
971	            missing = [i for i, r in enumerate(rids) if r is None]
972	            assert not missing, (
973	                f"Compact rollout returned {len(node)} samples but rollout_id is unset on "
974	                f"positions {missing}. Set Sample.rollout_id on every sibling so the loss "
975	                "reducer can aggregate them as one rollout instead of N."
976	            )
977	            assert len(set(rids)) == 1, f"Sibling samples from one compact rollout must share rollout_id; got {rids}."
978	        return
979	    for item in node:
980	        _validate_rollout_id_annotated(item, depth + 1)

983	def _allocate_rollout_engine_addr_and_ports_normal(
984	    *,
985	    args,
986	    rollout_engines,
987	    worker_type="regular",
988	    num_gpus_per_engine=None,
989	    rank_offset=0,
990	    base_port=15000,
991	):
992	    # get ports
993	    # there are 4 ports we need to allocate
994	    # 1. server port
995	    # 2. nccl port
996	    # 3. dist_init_addr port
997	    # 4. other ports for dp_attention, which is of size 4 + dp_size
998	    _gpus_per_engine = num_gpus_per_engine or args.rollout_num_gpus_per_engine
999	    num_engines_per_node = max(1, args.num_gpus_per_node // _gpus_per_engine)
1000	    addr_and_ports: dict[int, dict] = {}
1001	
1002	    # Track per-node port cursors so that different server groups (called
1003	    # sequentially) never race for the same ports on a given node.
1004	    node_port_cursor: dict[int, int] = {}
1005	
1006	    visited_nodes = set()
1007	    for rank, engine in rollout_engines:
1008	        local_rank = rank - rank_offset
1009	        node_index = local_rank // num_engines_per_node
1010	        if node_index in visited_nodes:
1011	            continue
1012	        visited_nodes.add(node_index)
1013	        # TODO: currently when restarting engines, we will set port for all engines on this node starting with this rank.
1014	        # e.g. for 8 gpus, if we are restarting engine on gpu 3, we will set port for engine 3,4,5,6,7 on this node.
1015	        num_engines_on_this_node = num_engines_per_node - (local_rank % num_engines_per_node)
1016	
1017	        def get_addr_and_ports(engine, node_idx):
1018	            # use small ports to prevent ephemeral port between 32768 and 65536.
1019	            # also, ray uses port 10002-19999, thus we avoid near-10002 to avoid racing condition
1020	            start_port = node_port_cursor.get(node_idx, base_port)
1021	
1022	            def port(consecutive=1):
1023	                nonlocal start_port
1024	                _, port = ray.get(
1025	                    engine._get_current_node_ip_and_free_port.remote(
1026	                        start_port=start_port,
1027	                        consecutive=consecutive,
1028	                    )
1029	                )
1030	                start_port = port + consecutive
1031	                node_port_cursor[node_idx] = start_port
1032	                return port
1033	
1034	            def addr():
1035	                addr, _ = ray.get(engine._get_current_node_ip_and_free_port.remote())
1036	                return addr
1037	
1038	            return addr, port
1039	
1040	        get_addr, get_port = get_addr_and_ports(engine, node_index)
1041	
1042	        for i in range(num_engines_on_this_node):
1043	            current_rank = rank + i
1044	            addr_and_ports.setdefault(current_rank, {})
1045	            addr_and_ports[current_rank]["host"] = get_addr()
1046	            addr_and_ports[current_rank]["port"] = get_port()
1047	            addr_and_ports[current_rank]["nccl_port"] = get_port()
1048	
1049	            if worker_type == "prefill":
1050	                addr_and_ports[current_rank]["disaggregation_bootstrap_port"] = get_port()
1051	
1052	        if _gpus_per_engine > args.num_gpus_per_node:
1053	            num_node_per_engine = _gpus_per_engine // args.num_gpus_per_node
1054	            if local_rank % num_node_per_engine == 0:
1055	                # this is the first node in the engine, we need to allocate the dist_init_addr port
1056	                dist_init_addr = f"{get_addr()}:{get_port(30 + args.sglang_dp_size)}"
1057	                for i in range(num_node_per_engine):
1058	                    addr_and_ports.setdefault(rank + i, {})
1059	                    addr_and_ports[rank + i]["dist_init_addr"] = dist_init_addr
1060	        else:
1061	            for i in range(num_engines_on_this_node):
1062	                addr_and_ports[rank + i]["dist_init_addr"] = f"{get_addr()}:{get_port(30 + args.sglang_dp_size)}"
1063	
1064	    for i, _ in rollout_engines:
1065	        for key in ["port", "nccl_port", "dist_init_addr"]:
1066	            assert key in addr_and_ports[i], f"Engine {i} {key} is not set."
1067	        logger.info(f"Ports for engine {i}: {addr_and_ports[i]}")
1068	
1069	    return addr_and_ports, node_port_cursor

1072	def _start_router(args, *, has_pd_disaggregation: bool = False, force_new: bool = False) -> tuple[str, int]:
1073	    """Start sglang_router and return (router_ip, router_port).
1074	
1075	    If ``args.sglang_router_ip`` is already set (e.g. by the user) and
1076	    ``force_new`` is False, skip launching and return the existing values.
1077	    When ``force_new`` is True (multi-model), always allocate a fresh port.
1078	    """
1079	    if not force_new and args.sglang_router_ip is not None:
1080	        return args.sglang_router_ip, args.sglang_router_port
1081	
1082	    router_ip = _wrap_ipv6(get_host_info()[1])
1083	    if force_new:
1084	        router_port = find_available_port(random.randint(3000, 4000))
1085	    else:
1086	        router_port = args.sglang_router_port
1087	        if router_port is None:
1088	            router_port = find_available_port(random.randint(3000, 4000))
1089	
1090	    from sglang_router.launch_router import RouterArgs
1091	
1092	    from slime.utils.http_utils import run_router
1093	
1094	    router_args = RouterArgs.from_cli_args(args, use_router_prefix=True)
1095	    router_args.host = router_ip
1096	    router_args.port = router_port
1097	    router_args.prometheus_port = find_available_port(random.randint(4000, 5000))
1098	    router_args.request_timeout_secs = args.sglang_router_request_timeout_secs
1099	
1100	    if has_pd_disaggregation:
1101	        router_args.pd_disaggregation = True
1102	
1103	    # Disable circuit breaker to prevent RDMA transfer timeouts from
1104	    # marking decode workers as dead. Timeouts are transient (PCIe
1105	    # contention under high load) and do not indicate a dead server.
1106	    router_args.disable_circuit_breaker = True
1107	
1108	    # We will not use the health check from router.
1109	    router_args.disable_health_check = True
1110	
1111	    logger.info(f"Launch router with args: {router_args}")
1112	
1113	    process = multiprocessing.Process(
1114	        target=run_router,
1115	        args=(router_args,),
1116	    )
1117	    process.daemon = True  # Set the process as a daemon
1118	    process.start()
1119	    # Wait 3 seconds
1120	    time.sleep(3)
1121	    assert process.is_alive()
1122	    logger.info(f"Router launched at {router_ip}:{router_port}, Prometheus port: {router_args.prometheus_port}")
1123	    return router_ip, router_port

1142	def start_rollout_servers(args, pg) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[Any]]:
1143	    """Start rollout servers without waiting for final engine initialization.
1144	
1145	    Each model defined in the sglang config gets its own router and set
1146	    of server groups.  Server groups within a model may have different
1147	    ``num_gpus_per_engine`` (e.g. for PD disaggregation where prefill
1148	    and decode use different TP sizes).
1149	
1150	    Returns ``(servers, init_handles)`` where servers maps model name to
1151	    ``RolloutServer`` and init_handles contains pending ``engine.init`` refs.
1152	
1153	    Note: ``init_http_client`` should be called separately before this,
1154	    as the HTTP client is shared across all servers.
1155	    """
1156	    if args.rollout_external:
1157	        return start_external_rollout_servers(args, start_router=_start_router)
1158	
1159	    config = _resolve_sglang_config(args)
1160	
1161	    servers: dict[str, RolloutServer] = {}
1162	    pending_init_handles: list[Any] = []
1163	    gpu_offset = 0
1164	    engine_offset = 0
1165	
1166	    # Compute megatron GPU range for per-group offload decisions.
1167	    rollout_pg_offset = _compute_rollout_offset(args)
1168	    megatron_num_gpus = _compute_megatron_num_gpus(args)
1169	
1170	    for model_idx, model_cfg in enumerate(config.models):
1171	        model_cfg.resolve(args)
1172	
1173	        has_pd = model_cfg.has_pd_disaggregation
1174	        router_ip, router_port = _start_router(args, has_pd_disaggregation=has_pd, force_new=(model_idx > 0))
1175	
1176	        # Write back for backward compat (first model only).
1177	        if model_idx == 0:
1178	            args.sglang_router_ip = router_ip
1179	            args.sglang_router_port = router_port
1180	
1181	        server_groups: list[ServerGroup] = []
1182	        port_cursors: dict[int, int] = {}
1183	
1184	        has_epd = model_cfg.has_encoder_disaggregation
1185	
1186	        def _make_group(group_cfg, router_ip, router_port, overrides_extra=None):
1187	            nonlocal engine_offset, gpu_offset
1188	            gpus_per_engine = group_cfg.num_gpus_per_engine
1189	            num_gpus_per_engine_on_node = min(gpus_per_engine, args.num_gpus_per_node)
1190	            num_engines = group_cfg.num_gpus // num_gpus_per_engine_on_node
1191	
1192	            group_abs_start = rollout_pg_offset + gpu_offset
1193	            needs_offload = args.offload_rollout and group_abs_start < megatron_num_gpus
1194	            overrides = dict(group_cfg.overrides)
1195	            if overrides_extra:
1196	                for k, v in overrides_extra.items():
1197	                    overrides.setdefault(k, v)
1198	            if args.offload_rollout and not needs_offload:
1199	                overrides.setdefault("enable_memory_saver", False)
1200	            logger.info(
1201	                f"Engine group '{group_cfg.worker_type}' gpu_offset={gpu_offset} "
1202	                f"(abs={group_abs_start}): needs_offload={needs_offload}"
1203	            )
1204	
1205	            group = ServerGroup(
1206	                args=args,
1207	                pg=pg,
1208	                all_engines=[None] * num_engines if group_cfg.worker_type != "placeholder" else [],
1209	                num_gpus_per_engine=gpus_per_engine,
1210	                num_new_engines=0,
1211	                worker_type=group_cfg.worker_type,
1212	                rank_offset=engine_offset,
1213	                gpu_offset=gpu_offset,
1214	                sglang_overrides=overrides,
1215	                needs_offload=needs_offload,
1216	                model_path=overrides.get("model_path", args.hf_checkpoint),
1217	                router_ip=router_ip,
1218	                router_port=router_port,
1219	            )
1220	            engine_offset += num_engines
1221	            gpu_offset += group_cfg.num_gpus
1222	            return group
1223	
1224	        if has_epd:
1225	            # --- Phase 1: start encoder groups, wait, collect URLs ---
1226	            # Encoder URLs are injected into the non-encoder workers' server args,
1227	            # so this phase must stay synchronous even though final LLM init is deferred.
1228	            encoder_urls: list[str] = []
1229	            for group_cfg in model_cfg.server_groups:
1230	                if group_cfg.worker_type != "encoder":
1231	                    continue
1232	                group = _make_group(group_cfg, router_ip, router_port)
1233	                handles, port_cursors = group.start_engines(port_cursors)
1234	                if handles:
1235	                    ray.get(handles)
1236	                urls = ray.get([e.get_url.remote() for e in group.engines])
1237	                encoder_urls.extend(u for u in urls if u is not None)
1238	                server_groups.append(group)
1239	
1240	            logger.info(f"EPD phase 1 done: collected {len(encoder_urls)} encoder URLs: {encoder_urls}")
1241	
1242	            # --- Phase 2: start non-encoder groups, injecting encoder URLs into
1243	            # language-only LLM workers. Prefill groups use this for full EPD,
1244	            # while regular groups allow encoder/LLM split without PD.
1245	            non_encoder_handles: list = []
1246	            for group_cfg in model_cfg.server_groups:
1247	                if group_cfg.worker_type == "encoder":
1248	                    continue
1249	                overrides_extra = {}
1250	                if encoder_urls and group_cfg.worker_type in ("prefill", "regular"):
1251	                    overrides_extra["language_only"] = True
1252	                    overrides_extra["encoder_urls"] = encoder_urls
1253	                group = _make_group(group_cfg, router_ip, router_port, overrides_extra=overrides_extra)
1254	                handles, port_cursors = group.start_engines(port_cursors)
1255	                non_encoder_handles.extend(handles)
1256	                server_groups.append(group)
1257	
1258	            pending_init_handles.extend(non_encoder_handles)
1259	        else:
1260	            # No EPD — start all groups in one pass (original path).
1261	            all_init_handles: list = []
1262	            for group_cfg in model_cfg.server_groups:
1263	                group = _make_group(group_cfg, router_ip, router_port)
1264	                handles, port_cursors = group.start_engines(port_cursors)
1265	                all_init_handles.extend(handles)
1266	                server_groups.append(group)
1267	
1268	            pending_init_handles.extend(all_init_handles)
1269	
1270	        servers[model_cfg.name] = RolloutServer(
1271	            server_groups=server_groups,
1272	            router_ip=router_ip,
1273	            router_port=router_port,
1274	            model_name=model_cfg.name,
1275	            update_weights=model_cfg.update_weights,
1276	        )
1277	
1278	    # Expose per-model router info for custom rollout functions.
1279	    args.sglang_model_routers = {name: (srv.router_ip, srv.router_port) for name, srv in servers.items()}
1280	
1281	    return servers, pending_init_handles

1321	        if (samples := data[key].get("samples")) is not None:
1322	            log_dict |= dict_add_prefix(compute_metrics_from_samples(args, samples), f"eval/{key}/")
1323	        if "truncated" in data[key]:
1324	            truncated = data[key]["truncated"]
1325	            log_dict[f"eval/{key}-truncated_ratio"] = sum(truncated) / len(truncated)
1326	        if args.log_passrate:
1327	            log_dict |= dict_add_prefix(
1328	                compute_pass_rate(
1329	                    flat_rewards=rewards,
1330	                    group_size=args.n_samples_per_eval_prompt,
1331	                ),
1332	                f"eval/{key}-",
1333	            )
1334	
1335	    logger.info(f"eval {rollout_id}: {log_dict}")
1336	
1337	    step = compute_rollout_step(args, rollout_id)
1338	    log_dict["eval/step"] = step
1339	    logging_utils.log(args, log_dict, step_key="eval/step")
1340	
1341	    return log_dict
1342	
1343	
1344	def _log_rollout_data(rollout_id, args, samples, rollout_extra_metrics, rollout_time):
1345	    if args.custom_rollout_log_function_path is not None:
1346	        custom_log_func = load_function(args.custom_rollout_log_function_path)
1347	        if custom_log_func(rollout_id, args, samples, rollout_extra_metrics, rollout_time):
1348	            return
1349	
1350	    if args.load_debug_rollout_data:
1351	        return
1352	
1353	    log_dict = {**(rollout_extra_metrics or {})}
1354	    log_dict |= dict_add_prefix(compute_metrics_from_samples(args, samples), "rollout/")
1355	    log_dict |= dict_add_prefix(compute_perf_metrics_from_samples(args, samples, rollout_time), "perf/")
1356	    logger.info(f"perf {rollout_id}: {log_dict}")
1357	    step = compute_rollout_step(args, rollout_id)
1358	    log_dict["rollout/step"] = step
1359	    logging_utils.log(args, log_dict, step_key="rollout/step")
1360	
1361	
1362	def compute_metrics_from_samples(args, samples):
1363	    response_lengths = [sample.effective_response_length for sample in samples]
1364	
1365	    log_dict = {}
1366	    log_dict |= dict_add_prefix(compute_statistics(response_lengths), "response_len/")
1367	    log_dict |= _compute_zero_std_metrics(args, samples)
1368	    log_dict |= _compute_spec_metrics(args, samples)
1369	    log_dict |= _compute_prefix_cache_metrics(args, samples)
1370	    log_dict |= _compute_reward_cat_metrics(args, samples)
1371	    log_dict |= _compute_top_p_kept_vocab_metrics(args, samples)
1372	    log_dict["repetition_frac"] = np.mean([int(has_repetition(s.response)) for s in samples]).item()
1373	    log_dict["truncated_ratio"] = np.mean([int(s.status == Sample.Status.TRUNCATED) for s in samples]).item()
1374	    return log_dict
1375	
1376	
1377	def compute_perf_metrics_from_samples(args, samples, rollout_time):
1378	    non_generation_time = [sample.non_generation_time for sample in samples]
1379	
1380	    log_dict = {}
1381	    log_dict["rollout_time"] = rollout_time
1382	    if max(non_generation_time) > 0:
1383	        log_dict |= dict_add_prefix(compute_statistics(non_generation_time), "non_generation_time/")
1384	
1385	    def token_perf(response_lengths, non_generation_time, key=""):
1386	        max_response_length = max(response_lengths)
1387	        if args.rollout_num_gpus:
1388	            log_dict[f"{key}tokens_per_gpu_per_sec"] = sum(response_lengths) / rollout_time / args.rollout_num_gpus
1389	        log_dict[f"longest_{key}sample_tokens_per_sec"] = max_response_length / rollout_time
1390	
1391	        if max(non_generation_time) == 0:
1392	            return
1393	
1394	        non_generation_time = [
1395	            t for t, length in zip(non_generation_time, response_lengths, strict=True) if length == max_response_length
1396	        ]
1397	        mean_non_generation_time = sum(non_generation_time) / len(non_generation_time)
1398	
1399	        log_dict[f"longest_{key}sample_non_generation_time"] = mean_non_generation_time
1400	        log_dict[f"longest_{key}sample_tokens_per_sec_without_non_generation"] = max_response_length / (
1401	            rollout_time - mean_non_generation_time
1402	        )
1403	
1404	    token_perf([sample.response_length for sample in samples], non_generation_time, key="")
1405	    token_perf([sample.effective_response_length for sample in samples], non_generation_time, key="effective_")
1406	    log_dict |= _compute_sglang_request_perf_metrics(samples)
1407	
1408	    return log_dict
1409	
1410	
1411	def _compute_sglang_request_perf_metrics(all_samples: list[Sample]):
1412	    attrs_by_request = list(_iter_sglang_generate_attrs(all_samples))
1413	    if not attrs_by_request:
1414	        return {}
1415	
1416	    values_by_metric: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
1417	    profiled_request_count = 0
1418	
1419	    def add_value(metric_key: str, source_key: str, attrs: dict) -> bool:
1420	        value = attrs.get(source_key)
1421	        if not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or isinstance(value, bool) or not np.isfinite(value):
1422	            return False
1423	        values_by_metric.setdefault(metric_key, []).append(float(value))
1424	        return True
1425	
1426	    for attrs in attrs_by_request:
1427	        request_has_perf = False
1428	
1429	        for metric_key, source_key in _SGLANG_REQUEST_PERF_FIELDS:
1430	            request_has_perf |= add_value(metric_key, source_key, attrs)
1431	
1432	        for metric_key, source_key in _SGLANG_PREFILL_PERF_FIELDS:
1433	            request_has_perf |= add_value(metric_key, source_key, attrs)
1434	
1435	        for metric_key, source_key in _SGLANG_DECODE_PERF_FIELDS:
1436	            request_has_perf |= add_value(metric_key, source_key, attrs)
1437	
1438	        if request_has_perf:
1439	            profiled_request_count += 1
1440	
1441	    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
1442	    for key, values in values_by_metric.items():
1443	        if not values:
1444	            continue
1445	        metrics |= dict_add_prefix(compute_statistics(values), f"{key}/")
1446	
1447	    return metrics
1448	
1449	
1450	def _iter_sglang_generate_attrs(all_samples: list[Sample]):
1451	    for sample in all_samples:
1452	        trace = getattr(sample, "trace", None)
1453	        if not isinstance(trace, dict):
1454	            continue
1455	        for event in trace.get("events") or []:
1456	            if event.get("type") != "span_end" or event.get("name") != "sglang_generate":
1457	                continue
1458	            attrs = event.get("attrs")
1459	            if isinstance(attrs, dict):
1460	                yield attrs
1461	
1462	
1463	def _compute_zero_std_metrics(args, all_samples: list[Sample]):
1464	    # only compute in GRPO-like algorithms where one prompt has multiple responses
1465	    if args.advantage_estimator == "ppo":
1466	        return {}
1467	
1468	    def _is_zero_std(samples: list[Sample]):
1469	        rewards = [sample.get_reward_value(args) for sample in samples]
1470	        return len(rewards) == 0 or all(rewards[0] == r for r in rewards)
1471	
1472	    all_sample_groups = group_by(all_samples, lambda s: s.group_index)
1473	    interesting_sample_groups = [g for g in all_sample_groups.values() if _is_zero_std(g)]
1474	
1475	    interesting_rewards = [str(round(g[0].get_reward_value(args), 1)) for g in interesting_sample_groups]
1476	
1477	    return {f"zero_std/count_{reward}": len(items) for reward, items in group_by(interesting_rewards).items()}
1478	
1479	
1480	def _compute_top_p_kept_vocab_metrics(args, all_samples: list[Sample]):
1481	    total_kept = 0
1482	    total_tokens = 0
1483	    for sample in all_samples:
1484	        offsets = sample.rollout_top_p_token_offsets
1485	        if offsets is None or sample.response_length == 0:
1486	            continue
1487	        offsets = torch.as_tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int64)
1488	        if offsets.numel() == 0:
1489	            continue
1490	        assert (
1491	            offsets.numel() == sample.response_length + 1
1492	        ), f"top-p token offsets length {offsets.numel()} != response length + 1 {sample.response_length + 1}"
1493	        if sample.remove_sample:
1494	            continue
1495	        if sample.loss_mask is None:
1496	            total_kept += int(offsets[-1] - offsets[0])
1497	            total_tokens += sample.response_length
1498	            continue
1499	        loss_mask = torch.as_tensor(sample.loss_mask, dtype=torch.bool, device=offsets.device)
1500	        assert (
1501	            loss_mask.numel() == sample.response_length
1502	        ), f"loss mask length {loss_mask.numel()} != response length {sample.response_length}"
1503	        total_kept += int(torch.diff(offsets)[loss_mask].sum())
1504	        total_tokens += int(loss_mask.sum())
1505	    if total_tokens == 0:
1506	        return {}
1507	    return {"top_p_kept_vocab_per_token": total_kept / total_tokens}
1508	
1509	
1510	def _compute_spec_metrics(args, all_samples: list[Sample]):
1511	    if getattr(args, "sglang_speculative_algorithm", None) is None:
1512	        return {}
1513	    num_samples = len(all_samples)
1514	    metrics = {}
1515	    metrics["spec_accept_rate"] = sum(sample.spec_info.spec_accept_rate for sample in all_samples) / num_samples
1516	    metrics["spec_accept_length"] = sum(sample.spec_info.spec_accept_length for sample in all_samples) / num_samples
1517	    return metrics
1518	
1519	
1520	def _compute_prefix_cache_metrics(args, all_samples: list[Sample]):
1521	    num_samples = len(all_samples)
1522	    metrics = {}
1523	    total_cached_tokens = sum(sample.prefix_cache_info.cached_tokens for sample in all_samples)
1524	    total_prompt_tokens = sum(sample.prefix_cache_info.total_prompt_tokens for sample in all_samples)
1525	
1526	    metrics["prefix_cache_hit_rate"] = total_cached_tokens / total_prompt_tokens if total_prompt_tokens > 0 else 0.0
1527	    metrics["avg_cached_tokens_per_sample"] = total_cached_tokens / num_samples
1528	    return metrics
1529	
1530	
1531	def _compute_reward_cat_metrics(args, all_samples: list[Sample]):
1532	    reward_cat_key = args.log_reward_category
1533	    if reward_cat_key is None:
1534	        return {}
1535	
1536	    samples_of_reward_cat = group_by(all_samples, lambda s: s.reward[reward_cat_key])
1537	
1538	    return {f"error_cat/{reward_cat}": len(s) / len(all_samples) for reward_cat, s in samples_of_reward_cat.items()}

57	    echo "==> QA parquet already present, skipping ($DATASET_DIR)"
58	    echo "    -> $train_parquet"
59	    echo "    -> $test_parquet"

123	  prepare_dataset

126	  prepare_corpus

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prepare the inputs for the Search-R1 slime recipe:
#   1. the QA dataset  -> nq_hotpotqa_train/{train,test}.parquet
#   2. the retrieval corpus -> wiki-18 e5 FAISS index + wiki-18.jsonl
#
# It drives the data-preparation subset of the Search-R1 repo that ships next to
# this recipe (workspace/Search-R1). Nothing here trains a model.
#
# Usage:
#   bash prepare_data.sh                 # dataset + corpus
#   DATASET_ONLY=1 bash prepare_data.sh  # skip the ~130GB corpus download
#   CORPUS_ONLY=1  bash prepare_data.sh  # only the retrieval corpus
#
# Override any path via the environment variables below.
set -euo pipefail

# --- locations -------------------------------------------------------------
# Directory of this script (examples/search-r1), resolved so it works from any cwd.
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# The trimmed Search-R1 repo. Defaults to the copy staged in this workspace
# (workspace/Search-R1); at container runtime the recipe reads /root/Search-R1,
# so allow an override.
SEARCH_R1_DIR="${SEARCH_R1_DIR:-$(cd "$HERE/../../Search-R1" && pwd)}"

# Where prepared assets land. Keep them inside the repo's data/ dir so the paths
# match the recipe's --prompt-data (…/Search-R1/data/nq_hotpotqa_train/…).
DATA_DIR="${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}"
DATASET_DIR="${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}"
CORPUS_DIR="${CORPUS_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/wiki-18}"

# Which QA sources to merge. Train mixes NQ+HotpotQA (the recipe default); the
# test merge can span more sets for evaluation.
TRAIN_SOURCES="${TRAIN_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"
TEST_SOURCES="${TEST_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"

DATASET_ONLY="${DATASET_ONLY:-0}"
CORPUS_ONLY="${CORPUS_ONLY:-0}"
# Re-download even if the target files already exist.
FORCE="${FORCE:-0}"

if [[ ! -d "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process" ]]; then
  echo "error: Search-R1 data-prep scripts not found under: $SEARCH_R1_DIR" >&2
  echo "       set SEARCH_R1_DIR to the trimmed Search-R1 repo." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# The merge scripts import verl.utils.hdfs_io from the repo root.
export PYTHONPATH="$SEARCH_R1_DIR${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

# --- 1) QA dataset ---------------------------------------------------------
prepare_dataset() {
  local train_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet"
  local test_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "==> QA parquet already present, skipping ($DATASET_DIR)"
    echo "    -> $train_parquet"
    echo "    -> $test_parquet"
    return
  fi

  echo "==> Building QA parquet into $DATASET_DIR"
  echo "    train sources: $TRAIN_SOURCES"
  echo "    test  sources: $TEST_SOURCES"
  mkdir -p "$DATASET_DIR"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "    train.parquet exists, skipping train merge"
  else
    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_train_merge.py" \
      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TRAIN_SOURCES"
  fi

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "    test.parquet exists, skipping test merge"
  else
    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py" \
      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TEST_SOURCES"
  fi

  echo "    -> $train_parquet"
  echo "    -> $test_parquet"
}

# --- 2) retrieval corpus (wiki-18 e5) --------------------------------------
prepare_corpus() {
  local index="$CORPUS_DIR/e5_Flat.index"
  local jsonl="$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$index" && -f "$jsonl" ]]; then
    echo "==> wiki-18 corpus already present, skipping ($CORPUS_DIR)"
    echo "    -> $index"
    echo "    -> $jsonl"
    return
  fi

  echo "==> Downloading wiki-18 e5 index + corpus into $CORPUS_DIR"
  echo "    NOTE: the assembled index is ~130GB; ensure disk + bandwidth."
  mkdir -p "$CORPUS_DIR"

  # Pulls PeterJinGo/wiki-18-e5-index (part_aa, part_ab) and
  # PeterJinGo/wiki-18-corpus (wiki-18.jsonl.gz) from the HuggingFace Hub.
  python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/download.py" --save_path "$CORPUS_DIR"

  echo "    Assembling e5_Flat.index from shards"
  cat "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_* > "$index"
  rm -f "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_*

  if [[ -f "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz" ]]; then
    echo "    Decompressing wiki-18.jsonl"
    gzip -df "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz"
  fi

  echo "    -> $index"
  echo "    -> $jsonl"
}

# --- run -------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$CORPUS_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
  prepare_corpus
elif [[ "$DATASET_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
  prepare_dataset
else
  prepare_dataset
  prepare_corpus
fi

echo "==> Done."

16	import random
17	import re
18	import string
19	
20	
21	def normalize_answer(s):
22	    def remove_articles(text):
23	        return re.sub(r"\b(a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
24	
25	    def white_space_fix(text):
26	        return " ".join(text.split())
27	
28	    def remove_punc(text):
29	        exclude = set(string.punctuation)
30	        return "".join(ch for ch in text if ch not in exclude)
31	
32	    def lower(text):
33	        return text.lower()
34	
35	    return white_space_fix(remove_articles(remove_punc(lower(s))))
36	
37	
38	def em_check(prediction, golden_answers):
39	    if isinstance(golden_answers, str):
40	        golden_answers = [golden_answers]
41	    normalized_prediction = normalize_answer(prediction)
42	    score = 0
43	    for golden_answer in golden_answers:
44	        golden_answer = normalize_answer(golden_answer)
45	        if golden_answer == normalized_prediction:
46	            score = 1
47	            break
48	    return score
49	
50	
51	def is_valid_sequence(text):
52	    # Find the position of "<|im_start|>assistant" with potential whitespace
53	    assistant_pattern = r"<\|im_start\|>assistant\s*"
54	    assistant_match = re.search(assistant_pattern, text)
55	
56	    if not assistant_match:
57	        return False, "Missing assistant marker"
58	
59	    # Extract the content after the assistant marker
60	    start_pos = assistant_match.end()
61	    content = text[start_pos:]
62	
63	    # Check for balanced tags
64	    tags_to_check = ["think", "search", "information", "answer"]
65	    for tag in tags_to_check:
66	        opening_count = len(re.findall(f"<{tag}>", content))
67	        closing_count = len(re.findall(f"</{tag}>", content))
68	        if opening_count != closing_count:
69	            return False, f"Mismatch in {tag} tags: {opening_count} opening vs {closing_count} closing tags"
70	
71	    # Now check for proper sequence pattern and no extraneous content
72	
73	    # 1. First split the content by any tags we recognize
74	    split_pattern = r"(</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>)"
75	    parts = re.split(split_pattern, content)
76	
77	    # 2. Keep track of the current position in the expected sequence
78	    state = "start"  # start -> think -> search -> information -> think -> ... -> answer -> end
79	
80	    # 3. Check each part
81	    for _i, part in enumerate(parts):
82	        # Skip empty parts
83	        if not part.strip():
84	            continue
85	
86	        # Check if this is a tag
87	        if re.match(r"</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>", part):
88	            # This is a tag, check if it's valid in the current state
89	            if part == "<think>" and state in ["start", "information"]:
90	                state = "in_think"
91	            elif part == "</think>" and state == "in_think":
92	                state = "after_think"
93	            elif part == "<search>" and state == "after_think":
94	                state = "in_search"
95	            elif part == "</search>" and state == "in_search":
96	                state = "after_search"
97	            elif part == "<information>" and state == "after_search":
98	                state = "in_information"
99	            elif part == "</information>" and state == "in_information":
100	                state = "information"
101	            elif part == "<answer>" and state == "after_think":
102	                state = "in_answer"
103	            elif part == "</answer>" and state == "in_answer":
104	                state = "end"
105	            else:
106	                return False, f"Unexpected tag {part} in state {state}"
107	        else:
108	            # This is content, check if it's valid in the current state
109	            if state in ["in_think", "in_search", "in_information", "in_answer"]:
110	                # Content is allowed inside tags
111	                pass
112	            elif state in ["start", "after_think", "after_search", "information"]:
113	                # Only whitespace is allowed between tags
114	                if part.strip():
115	                    return False, f"Unexpected content '{part.strip()}' between tags (state: {state})"
116	            else:
117	                return False, f"Unexpected content in state {state}"
118	
119	    # Check final state
120	    if state != "end":
121	        return False, f"Incomplete sequence, ended in state {state}"
122	
123	    return True, "Valid sequence format"
124	
125	
126	def extract_solution(solution_str):
127	    """Extract the equation from the solution string."""
128	
129	    answer_pattern = r"<answer>(.*?)</answer>"
130	    match = re.finditer(answer_pattern, solution_str, re.DOTALL)
131	    matches = list(match)
132	
133	    # If there are 0 or exactly 1 matches, return None
134	    if len(matches) <= 1:
135	        return None
136	
137	    # If there are 2 or more matches, return the last one
138	    return matches[-1].group(1).strip()
139	
140	
141	def extract_information_blocks(text: str) -> list[str]:
142	    pattern = r"<information>(.*?)</information>"
143	    matches = re.findall(pattern, text, re.DOTALL)
144	    return [match.strip() for match in matches]
145	
146	
147	def is_retrieval_correct(text: str, golden_answers: list[str]) -> list[str]:
148	    seqs = extract_information_blocks(text)
149	    for seq in seqs:
150	        for golden_answer in golden_answers:
151	            if normalize_answer(golden_answer) in normalize_answer(seq):
152	                return True
153	    return False
154	
155	
156	def compute_score_em(
157	    solution_str,
158	    ground_truth,
159	    method="strict",
160	    structure_format_score=0,
161	    final_format_score=0,
162	    retrieval_score=0,
163	    format_score=0,
164	    score=1.0,
165	):
166	    """The scoring function for exact match (EM).
167	
168	    Args:
169	        solution_str: the solution text
170	        ground_truth: the ground truth
171	        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
172	        format_score: the score for the format
173	        score: the score for the correct answer
174	    """
175	    is_valid_format, _ = is_valid_sequence(solution_str)
176	    retrieval_correct = False
177	    if is_valid_format:
178	        retrieval_correct = is_retrieval_correct(solution_str, ground_truth["target"])
179	    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str)
180	    do_print = random.randint(1, 64) == 1
181	
182	    if do_print:
183	        print("--------------------------------")
184	        print(f"Golden answers: {ground_truth['target']}")
185	        print(f"Extracted answer: {answer}")
186	        print(f"Solution string: {solution_str}")
187	
188	    if answer is None:
189	        if is_valid_format:
190	            if retrieval_correct:
191	                return structure_format_score + retrieval_score  # 0.3
192	            else:
193	                return structure_format_score  # 0.2
194	        else:
195	            return 0
196	    else:
197	        if em_check(answer, ground_truth["target"]):
198	            if is_valid_format:
199	                return score  # 1
200	            else:
201	                return score - structure_format_score  # 0.8
202	        elif is_valid_format:
203	            if retrieval_correct:
204	                return structure_format_score + retrieval_score  # 0.3
205	            else:
206	                return structure_format_score  # 0.2
207	        else:
208	            return final_format_score  # 0.1

21	def normalize_answer(s):
22	    def remove_articles(text):
23	        return re.sub(r"\b(a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
24	
25	    def white_space_fix(text):
26	        return " ".join(text.split())
27	
28	    def remove_punc(text):
29	        exclude = set(string.punctuation)
30	        return "".join(ch for ch in text if ch not in exclude)

32	    def lower(text):

38	def em_check(prediction, golden_answers):
39	    if isinstance(golden_answers, str):
40	        golden_answers = [golden_answers]
41	    normalized_prediction = normalize_answer(prediction)
42	    score = 0
43	    for golden_answer in golden_answers:
44	        golden_answer = normalize_answer(golden_answer)
45	        if golden_answer == normalized_prediction:
46	            score = 1
47	            break
48	    return score

51	def is_valid_sequence(text):
52	    # Find the position of "<|im_start|>assistant" with potential whitespace
53	    assistant_pattern = r"<\|im_start\|>assistant\s*"
54	    assistant_match = re.search(assistant_pattern, text)
55	
56	    if not assistant_match:
57	        return False, "Missing assistant marker"
58	
59	    # Extract the content after the assistant marker
60	    start_pos = assistant_match.end()
61	    content = text[start_pos:]
62	
63	    # Check for balanced tags
64	    tags_to_check = ["think", "search", "information", "answer"]
65	    for tag in tags_to_check:
66	        opening_count = len(re.findall(f"<{tag}>", content))
67	        closing_count = len(re.findall(f"</{tag}>", content))
68	        if opening_count != closing_count:
69	            return False, f"Mismatch in {tag} tags: {opening_count} opening vs {closing_count} closing tags"
70	
71	    # Now check for proper sequence pattern and no extraneous content
72	
73	    # 1. First split the content by any tags we recognize
74	    split_pattern = r"(</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>)"
75	    parts = re.split(split_pattern, content)
76	
77	    # 2. Keep track of the current position in the expected sequence
78	    state = "start"  # start -> think -> search -> information -> think -> ... -> answer -> end
79	
80	    # 3. Check each part
81	    for _i, part in enumerate(parts):
82	        # Skip empty parts
83	        if not part.strip():
84	            continue
85	
86	        # Check if this is a tag
87	        if re.match(r"</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>", part):
88	            # This is a tag, check if it's valid in the current state
89	            if part == "<think>" and state in ["start", "information"]:
90	                state = "in_think"
91	            elif part == "</think>" and state == "in_think":
92	                state = "after_think"
93	            elif part == "<search>" and state == "after_think":
94	                state = "in_search"
95	            elif part == "</search>" and state == "in_search":
96	                state = "after_search"
97	            elif part == "<information>" and state == "after_search":
98	                state = "in_information"
99	            elif part == "</information>" and state == "in_information":
100	                state = "information"
101	            elif part == "<answer>" and state == "after_think":
102	                state = "in_answer"
103	            elif part == "</answer>" and state == "in_answer":
104	                state = "end"
105	            else:
106	                return False, f"Unexpected tag {part} in state {state}"
107	        else:
108	            # This is content, check if it's valid in the current state
109	            if state in ["in_think", "in_search", "in_information", "in_answer"]:
110	                # Content is allowed inside tags
111	                pass
112	            elif state in ["start", "after_think", "after_search", "information"]:
113	                # Only whitespace is allowed between tags
114	                if part.strip():
115	                    return False, f"Unexpected content '{part.strip()}' between tags (state: {state})"
116	            else:
117	                return False, f"Unexpected content in state {state}"
118	
119	    # Check final state
120	    if state != "end":
121	        return False, f"Incomplete sequence, ended in state {state}"
122	
123	    return True, "Valid sequence format"

126	def extract_solution(solution_str):
127	    """Extract the equation from the solution string."""
128	
129	    answer_pattern = r"<answer>(.*?)</answer>"
130	    match = re.finditer(answer_pattern, solution_str, re.DOTALL)
131	    matches = list(match)
132	
133	    # If there are 0 or exactly 1 matches, return None
134	    if len(matches) <= 1:
135	        return None
136	
137	    # If there are 2 or more matches, return the last one
138	    return matches[-1].group(1).strip()
139

141	def extract_information_blocks(text: str) -> list[str]:
142	    pattern = r"<information>(.*?)</information>"
143	    matches = re.findall(pattern, text, re.DOTALL)
144	    return [match.strip() for match in matches]
145

147	def is_retrieval_correct(text: str, golden_answers: list[str]) -> list[str]:
148	    seqs = extract_information_blocks(text)
149	    for seq in seqs:
150	        for golden_answer in golden_answers:
151	            if normalize_answer(golden_answer) in normalize_answer(seq):
152	                return True
153	    return False

156	def compute_score_em(
157	    solution_str,
158	    ground_truth,
159	    method="strict",
160	    structure_format_score=0,
161	    final_format_score=0,
162	    retrieval_score=0,
163	    format_score=0,
164	    score=1.0,
165	):
166	    """The scoring function for exact match (EM).
167	
168	    Args:
169	        solution_str: the solution text
170	        ground_truth: the ground truth
171	        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
172	        format_score: the score for the format
173	        score: the score for the correct answer
174	    """
175	    is_valid_format, _ = is_valid_sequence(solution_str)
176	    retrieval_correct = False
177	    if is_valid_format:
178	        retrieval_correct = is_retrieval_correct(solution_str, ground_truth["target"])
179	    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str)
180	    do_print = random.randint(1, 64) == 1
181	
182	    if do_print:
183	        print("--------------------------------")
184	        print(f"Golden answers: {ground_truth['target']}")
185	        print(f"Extracted answer: {answer}")
186	        print(f"Solution string: {solution_str}")
187	
188	    if answer is None:
189	        if is_valid_format:
190	            if retrieval_correct:
191	                return structure_format_score + retrieval_score  # 0.3
192	            else:
193	                return structure_format_score  # 0.2
194	        else:
195	            return 0
196	    else:
197	        if em_check(answer, ground_truth["target"]):
198	            if is_valid_format:
199	                return score  # 1

201	                return score - structure_format_score  # 0.8

203	            if retrieval_correct:
204	                return structure_format_score + retrieval_score  # 0.3
205	            else:
206	                return structure_format_score  # 0.2
207	        else:
208	            return final_format_score  # 0.1

884	def vanilla_tis_function(
885	    args,
886	    *,
887	    pg_loss: torch.Tensor,
888	    train_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
889	    rollout_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
890	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
891	    **kwargs: Any,
892	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, list[torch.Tensor], dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
893	    rollout_log_probs = torch.cat(rollout_log_probs, dim=0)
894	    old_log_probs = torch.cat(train_log_probs, dim=0)
895	    tis = torch.exp(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs)
896	    tis_abs = (torch.exp(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs) - 1).abs()
897	    tis_weights = torch.clamp(tis, min=args.tis_clip_low, max=args.tis_clip)
898	    tis_clipfrac = (tis_weights != tis).float()
899	    metrics = {
900	        "tis": tis.clone().detach(),
901	        "tis_clipfrac": tis_clipfrac.clone().detach(),
902	        "tis_abs": tis_abs.clone().detach(),
903	    }
904	    pg_loss = pg_loss * tis_weights
905	    return pg_loss, loss_masks, metrics

918	    old_log_probs = torch.cat(train_log_probs, dim=0)
919	    ice_ratio = torch.exp(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs)
920	    ice_abs = (torch.exp(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs) - 1).abs()
921	    ice_weight = torch.where(

923	    )
924	    ice_clipfrac = (ice_weight != ice_ratio).float()
925	    metrics = {

927	        "tis_clipfrac": ice_clipfrac.clone().detach(),
928	        "tis_abs": ice_abs.clone().detach(),

1200	
1201	    _, values = get_values(

Replaces the legacy ``args.global_batch_size``\n            fallback so the train side stops depending on \"every DP rank holds\n            the same N samples\".\n        logits: Model outputs (policy or value head).\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple of `(scaled_loss, normalizer, logging_dict)` where:\n        - `scaled_loss` is the loss tensor (scalar) rescaled for Megatron.\n        - `normalizer` is `num_tokens` (scalar tensor) if\n          `args.calculate_per_token_loss` is True, else `1` (int).\n        - `logging_dict` has keys \"keys\" (list of str metric names) and\n          \"values\" (1D tensor: [count, metric1, metric2, ...]).\n    \"\"\"\n    num_tokens = sum([torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1) for loss_mask in batch[\"loss_masks\"]])\n\n    sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(\n        batch[\"total_lengths\"],\n        batch[\"response_lengths\"],\n        batch[\"loss_masks\"],\n        batch[\"rollout_mask_sums\"],\n        args.calculate_per_token_loss,\n    )\n\n    match args.loss_type:\n        case \"policy_loss\":\n            func = policy_loss_function\n        case \"value_loss\":\n            func = value_loss_function\n        case \"sft_loss\":\n            func = sft_loss_function\n        case \"custom_loss\":\n            func = load_function(args.custom_loss_function_path)\n        case _:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Unknown loss type: {args.loss_type}\")\n\n    if args.recompute_loss_function:\n        loss, log = checkpoint(func, args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean, use_reentrant=False)\n    else:\n        loss, log = func(args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean)\n\n    # With allgather-CP, some CP ranks may have no loss-contributing tokens (e.g., all\n    # padding). Adding this zero loss forces autograd to traverse the full\n    # graph on every rank without changing gradient values.\n    if args.allgather_cp and mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size() > 1:\n        loss = loss + 0 * logits.sum()\n\n    # Here we need to divide by cp_size because to cancel the multiply in Megatron.\n    if not args.calculate_per_token_loss:\n        loss = (\n            loss\n            * num_microbatches\n            / step_global_batch_size\n            * mpu.get_data_parallel_world_size(with_context_parallel=True)\n        )\n    else:\n        loss = loss * mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()\n\n    return (\n        loss,\n        (num_tokens if args.calculate_per_token_loss else torch.tensor(1, device=logits.device)),\n        {\n            \"keys\": list(log.keys()),\n            # values[0] is the consumer's reporting denominator after\n            # all-reduce.
